question:
Select the correct statements about religious beliefs of the Rig Vedic Period :
I. Dyus was a celestial God of the Rig Vedic Aryans similar to Jupiter of the Greeks.
II. Prithvi was considered as the mother of all Gods.
III. Agni was worshipped as the intermediary of taking the offerings to the deities.

Consider the following statements :

II. The Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills Case (1980) considered the extension of the scope of the second provision of Article 31C as invalid as well.
III. The Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills Case (1980) has considered the importance of harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
IV. The present interpretation with respect to the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is the same reiteration of the principle that was first propounded by the Supreme Court in the Chamapakan Dorairajan case (1951).
Which of the statement/statements given above is/are incorrect ?
explanation: Minerva Mills (1980) did stress harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, so statement III is correct. Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid with respect to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution ?
I. The term 'democratic' as used in the Preamble is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism.
II. The term 'Republic' in the Preamble indicates that India has an elected head, called the Prime Minister.
III. The 'Liberty' expressed in the Preamble is neither absolute nor qualified.
IV. The term 'Fraternity' as used by the Preamble, originally denoted the dignity of the individual only.

subject: AP History & Culture

question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect with reference to megalithic burials in Andhra ?
options: Tirupati has the largest anthropomorphic burial site collection
Many numbers of cyst burials were found in Vishakhapatnam District
Sarcophagus burials are more in number in Chittoor and Anantapuramu districts
Krishna and Chittoor districts contained many numbers of dolmen burials
explanation: Cist burials in Andhra are concentrated in the southern and Rayalaseema/Krishna regions, not in Visakhapatnam district, so statement (2) is the incorrect one.

subject: AP History & Culture
statement: In their inscriptions, Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had described themselves as the descendants of Ikshvakus of Ayodhya
question: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri ?
options: In their inscriptions, Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had described themselves as the descendants of Ikshvakus of Ayodhya
Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had matrimonial ties with Sakas/Western Satraps of Ujjain
Veerapurushadatta's reign is considered as the golden age of Buddhism in Andhra
explanation: The Ikshvaku inscriptions of Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) do not claim descent from the Ikshvakus of Ayodhya; that link was suggested by later scholars. The other three statements are accepted facts.

subject: AP History & Culture

They issued bilingual coins in Prakrit and Dravidian Script
They were patrons of Buddhism and Hinduism
They had matrimonial alliance with Kakatiyas

question:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct ?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet and the author of 'Andhra Mahabharatam', a Telugu retelling of the Sanskrit-language Mahabharata.
II. He is also credited with writing the Andhra Shabda Chintamani, a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.

explanation: Nannaya began the Andhra Mahabharatam and is traditionally credited with the Sanskrit grammar Andhra Sabda Chintamani. The Nandampudi grant of Rajaraja Narendra was made to Narayana Bhatta, not to Nannaya, so III is wrong.

subject: AP History & Culture

b. Raja Raja Narendra constructed Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole.

explanation: The Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole is attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's period, not to Rajaraja Narendra, so only b is incorrect. Vijayaditya II is credited with 108 Siva temples and Chalukya Bhima I with the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple.

subject: AP History & Culture

explanation: The key treats b as the only incorrect statement: the nayankara system is usually traced to earlier Kakatiya practice and was only expanded under Prataparudra. Statements a and c are accepted.

Which of the following statements regarding Library Movement are correct ?

question:
As per the provisions of Right to Information Act, the State Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, on the recommendations of a committee comprising of,
A. Chief Minister of the concerned State
B. Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court
C. Leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly
D. Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
explanation: Section 15(3) of the RTI Act names the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM; the High Court Chief Justice is not a member.

subject: Polity & Constitution
statement: The Lok Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
question:
The Parliament can make laws on subjects enumerated in the State list in the following conditions
A. On the request of two or more States.
B. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
C. Proclamation of International Agreements.
D. The Lok Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
explanation: Parliament can legislate on State subjects at the request of two or more States (Art. 252), on a Rajya Sabha resolution (Art. 249) and to implement international agreements (Art. 253). A Lok Sabha resolution has no such effect.

subject: Polity & Constitution
statement: The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
question:
Which of the following will be the correct consequences of declaration of National Emergency by the President ?
A. The President can modify the constitutional distribution of finances between the Center and the States.
B. The Center becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.
C. The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
explanation: During a national emergency the President can modify revenue sharing (Art. 354) and the Centre can direct States on any matter (Art. 353). Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, so C is wrong.

subject: Polity & Constitution
topic: High Courts, Subordinate Judiciary, Judicial Review, Activism and Pil
statement: PIL is an outcome of Judicial Restraint.
question:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is also known as Social Action Litigation.
B. PIL is an outcome of Judicial Restraint.
C. Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P. N. Bhagawathi were pioneers of the concept of PIL.

subject: Polity & Constitution
topic: Attorney General and Advocate General; Solicitor General
statement: He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
question:

i. The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney General of India.
ii. He shall have right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.
iii. He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
iv. He shall receive remuneration as the Parliament may determine.
explanation: Under Article 76 the AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge and has right of audience in all courts. He holds office at the pleasure of the President, not the PM, and his remuneration is fixed by the President, not Parliament.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the administration of tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution is/are correct ?
i. It is applicable in all States where Scheduled Tribes make up more than 40% of the State's population.
ii. These areas are outside the authority of the State Legislature as well as State Executive.
iii. Only the President can organise and reorganise the autonomous districts in these areas.
iv. The High Court of the State does not have any jurisdiction in these areas.
explanation: The Sixth Schedule applies only to tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The Governor, not the President, organises autonomous districts, and the State's executive and High Court still have jurisdiction. All four statements are wrong.

Which of the following is/are among the fundamental duties of citizens in the Indian Constitution ?
(i) To uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India.
(ii) To protect the weaker sections from social injustice.
(iii) To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
(iv) To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India.
Select the correct answer from the given code :
explanation: Upholding sovereignty, valuing the composite culture and promoting harmony are fundamental duties under Article 51A. Protecting the weaker sections from social injustice is a Directive Principle (Article 46).

question:
Consider the following statements about the Assam Movement :
I. The Assam Movement led by All Assam Students' Union (AASU) was started in the year 1983.
II. The objective of the Assam Movement is to identify the migrant people, protect and provide constitutional, legislative and administrative safeguards to the Bangladeshi Migrants in Assam.
III. The Assam Movement was officially ended on 15th August, 1989 after coming to an understanding with the Government of India which found official expression in the Memorandum of Understanding popularly known as the Assam Accord.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct ?
explanation: The AASU-led movement began in 1979, it aimed to detect and deport illegal migrants (safeguards were for the Assamese people, not the migrants), and it ended with the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985, so all three statements are wrong.
